topic: macOS Data Protection Keychain for Electron Apps: Securing AI Agent Credentials

key_points: Secure storage for signed Electron/Node apps backed by modern macOS Data Protection Keychain (kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain: true)
Protect items with code-signing access groups; share only with explicitly entitled apps (no security CLI access)
Restrict package access to declared item names (accounts/mutableAccounts); supports immutable + mutable accounts
Use SecItem API with kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain instead of legacy file-based Keychain
Optional device-owner auth (Touch ID / password via SecAccessControl), iCloud Keychain sync
Requires valid Apple code signature; uses host bundle identifier as Keychain service by default
Provides keychain-store npm package AND a Swift Package Manager KeychainStore library for native macOS targets
safeStorage encrypts/decrypts strings using OS cryptography; macOS key stored in Keychain Access under <AppName> Safe Storage
macOS encryption keys stored in a way that prevents other applications loading them without user override (code-signing required)
Windows uses DPAPI; Linux uses libsecret/kwallet with basic_text hardcoded-password fallback
safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() returns true on macOS if Keychain is available
safeStorage.getSelectedStorageBackend() returns basic_text when no secret store available (unprotected, hardcoded password)
Keychain access calls can block the current thread collecting user input
safeStorage is a ~100-line C++ wrapper over Chromium OSCrypt — no own crypto; inherits all Chromium baggage
OSCrypt uses AES-128-CBC with a HARDCODED IV (16 spaces); identical plaintext -> identical ciphertext; no GCM/auth
macOS is the strongest platform: Keychain entry protected by system ACL, prompts for authorization, encrypted DB even offline
Child processes / injected libraries / malicious npm packages are treated as the app itself and can decrypt without prompting
Linux basic_text fallback is plaintext-equivalent (PBKDF2-1-iteration + 'saltysalt' hardcoded salt + hardcoded password) and is the DEFAULT fallback
VS Code case: any extension can read all secrets because Electron apps don't sandbox extensions (same process, one Keychain ACL)
VoidStealer (2026-03) steals master key via debugger attach / hardware breakpoint when app calls decryptString
DPAPI (Windows) is per-user, not per-app: any process as same user can decrypt — no prompt, no isolation
macOS Keychain has per-application ACL: rogue same-user process gets a Keychain prompt, unlocks only that binary path
Linux libsecret/kwallet protects per-user, not per-app (similar to Windows)
Ask 'encrypted against whom?' — DPAPI vs other users, macOS Keychain vs other apps (meaningfully better), hardware-backed stores vs the OS itself
For AI agents running untrusted code, per-user stores are effectively readable by that code
Practical keytar->safeStorage migration in Ray (Spatie debugging app) using electron-store for ciphertext persistence
safeStorage avoids native-module build pain of keytar (no per-platform compilation)
Pattern: safeStorage.encryptString(password) -> store Buffer as latin1 string; decrypt on read
Migration caveat: old keytar entries inaccessible after switch; use electron-store migrations to flag users to re-enter credentials
Note they used electron-store encryptionKey 'this_only_obfuscates' — a weak obfuscation, not real security

stats.fact: macOS Keychain entries are encrypted even when the disk is stolen, unless the user has no login password set
safeStorage (Chromium OSCrypt) uses AES-128-CBC with a hardcoded IV of 16 space characters, not random per encrypt — enabling ciphertext comparison and CBC padding-oracle/bit-flipping attacks

On Linux without libsecret/kwallet, Electron falls back to basic_text which is plaintext-equivalent (PBKDF2-1-iteration, hardcoded 'saltysalt' salt and source password), and this is the DEFAULT fallback with no warning

VoidStealer (disclosed by Kaspersky March 2026) steals the encryption master key by attaching a debugger with a hardware breakpoint when the app calls its decryption API — no admin, no injection, no EDR trip; key briefly lives in process memory

macOS Data Protection Keychain (kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain) supports code-signing entitlement access groups, iCloud Keychain sync, and biometric (Touch ID) access control — none supported by the legacy file-based Keychain

VS Code SecretStorage ultimately calls safeStorage and stores ciphertext in ${HOME}/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb; any extension (full Node privileges, no sandbox) can read the DB and decrypt every secret via libsecret/keytar fork/CryptUnprotectData + hardcoded IV

angles: The show-HN 'keychain-store' library (biwills/biw) from ~June 2026 is the lead example — built specifically because safeStorage's legacy file-based keychain can be queried by other agents via the `security` CLI, which is dangerous when a dozen AI agents run in the background
Threat model framing: ask 'encrypted against whom?' — DPAPI per-user vs macOS Keychain per-app vs hardware-backed per-OS; this is the differentiator for AI-agent credential storage
The macOS Data Protection Keychain is meaningfully stronger than safeStorage for AI agents because code-signing access groups keep other agents/apps out and let you add Touch ID/password gating

"Encrypted ≠ done worrying": safeStorage's hardcoded IV and Linux basic_text fallback mean 'secure' apps leak credentials to anything that can read a file — dangerous when storing OpenAI/Anthropic API keys or JWTs
Electron apps don't sandbox extensions/code — any runnable code (malicious npm package, extension, mod) is treated as the app itself and can decrypt keys without a prompt
Cross-platform reality: Data Protection Keychain is macOS-only; the library falls back to safeStorage on Linux/Windows, preserving Electron's cross-platform promise with the strongest macOS option
